video_title: Modular Monolith: Logical Separation Without Physical Distribution
core_insight: A modular monolith gives you the developer speed of a monolith with enforced module boundaries, letting you defer microservices until you have proven need for independent scale or deploy.

scenes.voice: Why do successful apps suddenly feel slow to change? The code works, but every feature touches everything.
scenes.visual: Developer looking at tangled code lines, then a big ball of mud diagram forming.

scenes.voice: A layered monolith is fast at first. As it grows, changes in one feature break unrelated features, tests take minutes, onboarding drags.
scenes.visual: Simple layered boxes growing into a tangled mesh.

scenes.voice: Microservices fix coupling, but they bring network latency, distributed transactions, separate deploys, and ops overhead. For many products, that cost is too high early on.
scenes.visual: Boxes split into separate services with network lines, latency icons.

scenes.voice: So what if you want logical separation without physical distribution? That's a modular monolith: one deployable app with enforced internal boundaries.
scenes.visual: Single app box containing distinct module districts.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph App [Single Deployable Application]
        direction TB
        UI[Web/API Layer]
        subgraph Modules
            direction LR
            Billing[Billing Module]
            Catalog[Catalog Module]
            Orders[Orders Module]
        end
        DB[(Single Database)]
    end
    UI --> Billing
    UI --> Catalog
    UI --> Orders
    Billing --> Orders
    Orders --> Catalog
    Billing --> DB
    Catalog --> DB
    Orders --> DB

scenes.voice: Each module owns its domain model and exposes a public API. Tools like ArchUnit forbid imports except via that API. No direct access to internals, dependencies are one-directional.
scenes.visual: Module boxes with public API gate, red cross on direct internal access.

scenes.voice: You keep one repo, one database, one deploy, and local transactions. You gain clarity and faster delivery. The trade-off: you can't scale Billing independently of Catalog, and a bug can affect the whole process.
scenes.visual: Scale arrow up for whole app, warning icon for blast radius.

scenes.voice: Think city with districts, not independent cities. Design modules as future services. Extract to microservices only when you prove need for independent deploy cadence, scaling, or team ownership.
scenes.visual: City map with districts, then one district lifts out as a service.

mental_model: A city with districts inside one city limits. Modules are cohesive business capabilities with private internals and a published API, enforced by architectural tests. You get monolith operational simplicity with service-like clarity, and each module is a candidate for future extraction.
final_takeaway: Use a modular monolith when you need logical boundaries now and physical boundaries maybe later. Enforce module APIs with tests, and extract only when independent scale or deploy is proven.
